Package edu.cnu.mdi.splot.io

Class CsvPlotIO

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.splot.io.CsvPlotIO
public final class CsvPlotIO extends Object
Import and export of XY curve data as CSV, for exchange with tools that do not know the .plot.json format (spreadsheets, pandas, gnuplot, R).

CSV carries data only: curve names, their points and optional errors, plus the plot title and axis labels as optional header comments. Styling, axis limits, fits and everything else belong to the .plot.json format (PlotIO); importing a CSV therefore produces a plot with default formatting. Only XY plots are supported; histograms are not.

Export format

The "long" layout, one point per row, which also handles curves with different x values:

 # title: Beam profile
 # xlabel: Position (mm)
 # ylabel: Counts
 curve,x,y,e
 run 1,0.0,3.5,0.2
 run 1,1.0,4.1,0.2
 run 2,0.0,2.9,0.3

The e column (the y error) appears only when the plot has errors. Numbers are written with full precision, so a save followed by a load reproduces the data exactly.

Accepted on import

  • Long layout as above. The header must be curve,x,y or curve,x,y,e (name or series may replace curve). Rows with the same curve name form one curve, in order of first appearance.
  • Wide layout: a header row x,name1,name2,... with one shared x column and one column per curve. A blank cell means "no point for this curve at this x".
  • No header: if the first row is numeric the file is read as the wide layout, with curves named Curve 1, Curve 2, ...

Fields may be quoted per RFC 4180. Lines starting with # are comments; title:, xlabel: and ylabel: comments set the plot's labels and any other comment is ignored. Values must be finite numbers; anything else is rejected with the offending line number rather than guessed at.

    • loadCanvas

      public static PlotCanvas loadCanvas(File file) throws IOException
      Reads a CSV file and builds a new plot from it. The plot title defaults to the file name without its extension, and the axis labels to the x column's header (or "X") and "Y". Construction happens on the event thread.
      Parameters:
      file - the CSV file
      Returns:
      a new, un-started canvas
      Throws:
      IOException - if the file cannot be read or is not valid CSV data
